5.0.s.en: (1) The ark of the covenant in Ashdod

5.0.0.en: Ashdod: one of the important cities of the Philistines, lying north of the city of Gaza.

5.0.1.en: Dagon: a god worshipped by the Philistines, the Assyrians and the Phoenicians. He is the god of wheat and agricultural crops, and is called the god of fertility. His head, chest and arms were in the form of a man, while the rest of his body was in the form of a fish, because of the great multiplication of fish in the sea.

5.0.2.en: The Israelites left the ark of the covenant at the place of battle and fled, so the Philistines took it to one of their famous cities, Ashdod. They found no better place to put the ark than the temple devoted to one of their famous gods, the idol Dagon, so the ark was beside the statue of the god. In this they displayed the power of their god Dagon, whom they considered the greatest of their gods, since they brought to him the ark of the covenant of God, the God of Israel, whom they thought weak because they had prevailed over Him and His people. They placed it before Dagon, but Dagon, in whom there was a demon, could not bear to see God, and fell on his face before Him, as we shall see in the following verses.

5.1.0.en: On the morning of the first day, after the ark entered the temple of "Dagon," the pagan Philistine priests rose early to stand before their god, and to their surprise they found the statue of Dagon fallen on its face, that is, prostrate! This was a strange thing that had never happened to their statue, so they could do nothing but set it up again in its place. The next day they entered the temple of Dagon to worship, and behold, he was fallen on his face again as the day before, but this time the fall was more severe, for after he fell on his face his head and his hands were severed on the threshold of the temple. This means that the head, which symbolizes the mind, and the hands, which symbolize work, did not belong to this god, that is, he has no mind and is powerless to do anything, and the animal part, the fish, remained to declare the lowliness of this god. In addition, the falling of the head and hands at the threshold, which is trodden by feet, also declares the lowliness of this god and the shame of whoever worships him.

5.1.1.en: God also declares His power to the pagans. Although He had departed from His people because of their evils, He glorifies His name before those who are far off, that they may believe in Him.

5.1.2.en: And when God, whom the ark of the covenant signifies, enters the heart, all the powers of the world, of position and money .., are shattered before Him.

5.2.0.en: Instead of understanding, realizing and acknowledging that this "Dagon" was nothing but the work of human hands, the priests of "Dagon" went in another strange direction, adding undeserved honor to their stone god. They took a vow upon themselves that their feet would not tread on the threshold of the house, out of respect for the fall of his head and hands on the threshold!! This tradition continued for many years.

5.3.0.en: Tumors: some think it was not the well-known disease of hemorrhoids but the result of the plague, which strikes the lymph glands and the groin. This disease is carried by rats, so the Septuagint declares that rats attacked the land of the Philistines, and it is stated in (v. 11) that they feared death, because of the epidemic of plague.

5.3.1.en: Since the Philistines did not understand the divine purpose of these blows to their god and their pride, "Dagon," the Lord God made His hand heavy upon them, afflicting them with distress, ruin and lack of blessing in the matters of their material life. Moreover, the Lord added to that by striking them with the very painful disease of tumors, which causes severe distress to the one who has it.

5.4.0.en: Finally the people of Ashdod understood and grasped the lesson, and realized that the God of Israel was behind all these blows, and they reached a decision that the ark of the God of Israel could not remain with them. What had befallen them with their god was enough for them on the one hand, and they also feared what was coming upon them.

5.4.1.en: It took a long time for the people of Ashdod to understand ... Be quick to understand God's purposes, and return at once with repentance and apology and resolve to amend, and you will save yourself from God's disciplines and enjoy a calm, blessed life.

5.5.1.en: Gath: one of the large cities of the Philistines like Ashdod, lying northeast of Gaza.

5.5.2.en: The leaders of the Philistine clans gathered after the amazing events at Ashdod, and the purpose of the meeting was one thing: what shall we do with the ark of the covenant and where shall we put it? The opinion was that they should move it to the city of Gath, and in this they proved their lack of understanding, for they thought that the God of Israel did not like Ashdod or Dagon, so they proposed an alternative place.

5.6.1.en: The hand of the Lord was also on the city of "Gath," as it had been on Ashdod, so the same affliction of distress and turmoil struck them, and the tumors broke out and they had the same pain. God allowed these pains and did not destroy them because they had taken the ark of God's covenant in ignorance, not knowing that it was God.

5.6.2.en: When afflictions recur with you, examine yourself and pray to understand God's purposes, for His aim may be to call you to repent of a certain sin or to correct a certain shortcoming.

5.7.0.en: Ekron: a famous Philistine city lying south of "Joppa," and its meaning is "barren."

5.7.1.en: To rid themselves of the ark and its troubles, the people of "Gath" made a decision to send the ark away from them and send it to the city of Ekron, without the permission or knowledge of the Ekronites. For this reason the people of Ekron cried out, murmured and were afraid when the ark reached them, and said, The people of "Gath" have sent the ark to us for our destruction. The First Book of Samuel

5.8.0.en: As soon as the ark arrived, the people of Ekron sensed God's vengeance and His strong hand, for there was great turmoil because of the rising number of the dead. For this reason they held a meeting of all the leaders of the Philistine clans and asked that the ark return to Israel, to its place and its rest, so that the very severe vengeance of the God of Israel might stop.

5.9.0.en: Death struck some, while the rest were struck with the disease of tumors, and the pain was severe and the distress great, so that the cry of the people filled the whole city, crying for help to have the ark removed from them.

5.9.1.en: God may allow His children some discipline, as happened with Israel His people because of laxity and recklessness, but for the sake of the glory of His name God does not allow the enemies to gloat over His children or enjoy victory. He is just and repays with right, and at the same time He is jealous for His name and for His people. So do not wrong anyone and rejoice in what you have gained, for God is able to repay you with many blows if you do not repent. The return of the ark of God

6.0.0.en: The ark of God's covenant was lost in the war of the children of Israel against the Philistines, at Ebenezer, then it was moved to the Philistine city of "Ashdod," and from there to "Gath," then to "Ekron," and this took a period of seven months. The strange thing is that the people of Israel did not try anything in that time to recover the ark, whether by war or paying money or any kind of negotiation, as if the matter meant nothing. But we understand from this the state of the people, in spiritual heedlessness and strange resignation.

6.0.1.en: The stay of the ark of God's covenant in the land of the Philistines was long for several reasons:

6.0.2.en: 1- So that the Philistines might understand that the blows that came upon them were not chance but from the God of Israel.

6.0.3.en: 2- So that the Philistines might know that the God of Israel is stronger than their gods, indeed that He is the God of gods.

6.0.4.en: 3- So that the children of Israel might feel their sins that caused God to forsake them, and repent and keep His commandments.

6.1.0.en: The priests: they are the priests of the gods of the Philistines such as Dagon and Beelzebub.

6.1.1.en: The diviners: they claim knowledge of the unseen, and Satan may help them in some matters to extend his influence. God is the defender of His glory and of His name, so after He struck the Philistines with all these blows, He moved them to gather their priests and also the diviners to advise the people what to do with the ark of the covenant and how to return it to the Israelites. God does not leave Himself without a witness, and He uses even the pagans and moves them to bear witness to Him.

6.2.0.en: The first suggestion of the priests and diviners was to send an offering of appeasement to the God of Israel, which they called a "trespass offering," as a kind of apology for what they had committed by their theft of the ark. When sending this offering they expected that the God of Israel would have mercy on them and heal their sickness, so that the Philistines would be sure that all these diseases were because of their wrong against the God of Israel.

6.3.1.en: The people asked the priests and diviners for their suggestion of the suitable offering, and their answer was that they should make five images in the form of the tumors, which was the disease that afflicted them, and five images in the form of rats, because among God's blows on them mentioned here was the increase in the number of rats that ate most of their crops and made their homes ruins. By this they would appease the Lord God of Israel so that He would lift His anger from the people and from the land. The suggestion of the number five was based on the fact that the main cities of Philistia and the leaders of their clans were five, and so the whole people would share in the offering and the apology.

6.3.2.en: We notice that the atonement and apology of the Philistines for their sin against the ark of God's covenant shows the following:

6.3.3.en: 1- That it resembles what happened when the children of Israel left Egypt, when they took the gold and silver from the Egyptians.

6.3.4.en: 2- That the pagans' concept of atonement for sin is paying a sum of money, whereas atonement, as the Bible declares, is accomplished only by the blood of Christ, to which the blood of the sacrifices in the Old Testament pointed.

6.4.0.en: Why do you harden your hearts?!: a question whose purpose is prohibition, that is, do not harden your hearts.

6.4.1.en: The priests and diviners completed their words by giving advice to the leaders of the Philistines, which was to obey what they said and not make light of their words. They reminded them of the history of the children of Israel and how the great God of Israel struck Pharaoh of Egypt with the ten plagues until he let them go against his will.

6.4.2.en: God's power appears here in how He moved the pagan priests and diviners to bear witness to Him and to declare their wrong against Him when they stole His ark. So they offered trespass offerings that He might forgive them and heal their diseases, and they believed in His power that struck the Egyptians with the ten plagues. All this is a call to believe in God, that perhaps some of the pious among the people would believe in Him, for God does not leave Himself without a witness in every place, even in places where you do not expect anyone to be found bearing witness to His holy name. For they declared that He is a God stronger than their gods and cannot be resisted, as all the gods of the Egyptians could not resist Him. It is understood of course that the gifts were not a bribe to God but atonement for their sins against Him.

6.4.3.en: Here appears the virtue of the Philistine priests in learning from the sins of the Egyptians, who opposed the God of Israel so that the ten plagues came upon them, so they decided to submit and apologize to Him. How beautiful it is to learn from the sins of others and be careful not to fall into them.

6.5.1.en: Beth Shemesh: the first Jewish city after the borders of the Philistines, lying in the southeast of the tribe of Judah.

6.5.2.en: The yoke: a rod of wood placed on the necks of two animals to pull agricultural implements or wagons. By chance: by coincidence.

6.5.3.en: The priests and diviners suggested making a wooden cart with the ark of the covenant placed on it, and another chest carrying the golden tumors and rats. They stipulated that the cart be new, and in this was honor to the ark and the God of Israel, and that the two cows be nursing and their young (the little calves) be left in the pen, and also that they had never pulled any cart or agricultural implement before, "on which a yoke has never come." But why?!

6.5.4.en: The priests wanted to determine one thing: whether these blows were from the God of Israel or were merely chance!! For this reason they set difficult conditions.

6.5.5.en: A nursing cow cannot walk while leaving her suckling behind her; this is almost impossible. Likewise a cow on whose back a yoke has never come, and which has not been used before to pull carts, would find it hard to pull the cart toward Israel on a steep, difficult and untrodden road, having no experience in drawing carts without a man to lead her and direct her .. So after all that, if the two cows headed toward the Jewish city of Beth Shemesh, it would mean that the God of Israel was behind all that had befallen them, but if the two cows returned to them and did not go, it would all be chance and the God of Israel had no part in it.

6.5.6.en: The new cart and the two cows that had not been used in farm work signify that we must worship God with all the heart, and the heart must not be occupied with or rely on the things of the world, nor should a person keep God in his heart while being lax toward sin or the passing preoccupations of the world.

6.6.0.en: The Philistines did exactly what the priests and diviners had suggested, in choosing the two cows and shutting up their calves, and they placed the ark of the covenant of the Lord on the cart, and beside it the chest of the offering containing the images of the rats and the tumors.

6.7.0.en: Lowing: crying out in a loud voice.

6.7.1.en: The two cows went in a straight line to the Jewish city of Beth Shemesh, without turning to the right or the left, and their voice was loud, perhaps because they had left their young. Behind the wooden cart some of the Philistines walked to make sure that the cart reached Beth Shemesh.

6.7.2.en: If affliction comes upon you, examine yourself and offer repentance, lest your sins be the cause of what has come upon you; and accept the affliction from the hand of God and seek His help, for He is a tender Father ready to forgive you, support you and turn the affliction into a blessing.

6.8.s.en: (2) The arrival of the ark among the children of Israel

6.8.0.en: The valley: low land between two high places.

6.8.1.en: The harvest began at the Feast of Pentecost and lasted about two months (May and June). During this period, while the wheat was being harvested in the fields, the people of the city of Beth Shemesh caught sight of the cart carrying the ark, and their joy was great when they saw it, and they felt God's pleasure with them as He returned to dwell in their midst. Here appears the love of God, who seeks His children in order to dwell among them despite their laziness and their laxity in seeking His dwelling among them.

6.9.0.en: The two cows and the cart stopped at the house of a man named "Joshua," and beside his house was a large stone. The Israelites took the cart and cut up its wood to be fuel and kindled it on the stone, then they slaughtered the two cows and offered them up as a burnt offering to the Lord. They broke up the cart and used its wood as fuel because it was not right to use it for anything after it had carried the ark of God's covenant, since it had become holy to Him.

6.10.0.en: Since it was forbidden for any of the people to touch the ark, the Levites came and took down the ark, and placed it and the chest that was with it on the large stone. In expression of joy, the people of Beth Shemesh offered other burnt offerings and sacrifices in thanks to the Lord for His great work and how He had returned the ark to them.

6.11.0.en: As for the leaders of the Philistines who followed the cart and the two cows from a distance, after making sure that the ark had reached Beth Shemesh, they returned to the Philistine city of Ekron on the same day.

6.11.1.en: It is strange that after the leaders of the Philistines were sure that the God of Israel is stronger than their gods and also the gods of the Egyptians, and after they felt the diseases that had fallen on them, and then the ark's return by its own power to its people, all this did not draw them to believe in Him more than in their gods. This still happens even now, a proof of the stubbornness of man's heart and his rejection of the voice of God .. But you, do not be stubborn if God reveals to you any spiritual truth.

6.11.2.en: It was natural that the Israelites were unable to recover the ark, but what man is unable to do, God completes for him. Be faithful and do what is within your power, and leave the rest of the matters to the Lord Christ, who governs all and who alone is able to complete your human weakness!!

6.12.0.en: A village of the open country: a village without walls.

6.12.1.en: These two verses speak about the gifts presented by the leaders or rulers of the five great Philistine cities, and here the names of these cities are mentioned: (Gaza, Ashdod, Gath, Ashkelon and Ekron). These gifts consisted of five golden images in the form of tumors, while the golden rats were far more numerous, for five of them were for the five cities, and every village also offered a golden rat besides the five cities, because the rats had spread in the cities and villages. The prophet Samuel adds in his record of these events that the large stone which was used as an altar and on which the ark was afterward placed is still a witness to all these events, standing in its place in the field of "Joshua" the Beth Shemite.

6.13.s.en: (3) The striking of the people of "Beth Shemesh"

6.13.0.en: The ark of the covenant had three coverings (see Num 4:3-6), so that no one would look at it or gaze at its contents. But when the ark reached the town of Beth Shemesh, the people came from every place to gaze at the ark, and perhaps they uncovered its coverings or even opened it to see what was inside. The greatest error was that they did not return the ark to its place in the tabernacle. So the hand of the Lord was heavy upon them, and fifty thousand and seventy men died. Of course this whole number was not from the town of Beth Shemesh, since it is a small town, but from the whole people, because they dared to look at it and did not take care to return it to its place. So there was sorrow and mourning because of this great blow. God punished the lax among the Jews with death because they knew the holiness of the ark and were lax, whereas He did not kill the Philistines who looked at the ark but only struck them with diseases, because they did not believe in the God of Israel and did not know how to treat His ark. In addition, the Philistines had honored the ark by placing it on a new cart drawn by two cows that had not worked before, whereas the lax Jews put it on a stone in the open air and did not return it to the tabernacle of meeting or put it temporarily inside a room set aside for it, covered. This signifies what some Christians do now who approach Communion without repentance or while persisting in their sins, for laxity toward this sacrament angers God greatly.

6.14.0.en: Kirjath Jearim: a village 14.5 km west of Jerusalem, lying on a place higher than the village of Beth Shemesh, as shown by his saying "come down" to the inhabitants of Kirjath Jearim.

6.14.1.en: The people of Beth Shemesh cried out and acknowledged that they were sinners and could not stand before God (and who can?), and asked that the ark of the covenant be moved away from them (taken up), but to where and to whom should it go?! So they sent messengers to the village of Kirjath Jearim, asking them to come and take the ark from their town, and the people of the town responded, as we shall understand from the next chapter. Their thinking was how to be rid of the ark out of fear of it, whereas it would have been more fitting for them to offer repentance to God and be reconciled with Him, seeking to please Him by placing it in the proper place and honoring it as it ought to be.

6.14.2.en: They sent the ark to the town of Kirjath Jearim and not to Shiloh, where the tabernacle of meeting was, because the Philistines had destroyed it. Samuel afterward set up the tabernacle in the city of Nob and placed in it the vessels and the altar, and the ark remained in Kirjath Jearim until David moved it (1 Chr 15:4-15, 2 Chr 1:4).

6.14.3.en: The children of Israel dared to look at the ark of God and did not hallow it as the Law prescribed by not looking at it, and this led to their destruction. How much more, then, he who is lax and approaches the Holy Mysteries in the New Testament without repentance deserves a greater punishment. May you prepare with repentance, prayer and purification to receive the power of Communion from the Body and Blood of the Lord.

6.14.4.en: The settling of the ark, the repentance of the people, and the defeat of the Philistines
